scenes.heading: Retry Mechanisms
scenes.narration: Retry mechanisms automatically re-attempt failed operations so temporary problems resolve themselves without human intervention.

scenes.heading: Elements of a good retry
bullets: A cap on the number of attempts.
Jitter to avoid synchronized retry storms.
Idempotent operations so retries are safe.
scenes.narration: You limit attempts so a doomed operation eventually gives up instead of looping forever. Exponential backoff spaces retries further apart, giving the downstream system room to recover. Jitter randomizes the timing so many clients do not retry in lockstep, and idempotency ensures a repeated call causes no double effects.

scenes.heading: The retry loop
scenes.narration: Each attempt either succeeds or fails, and only transient failures trigger a retry. Between tries the client waits, extending the delay exponentially and sprinkling in randomness. This continues until the call succeeds or the attempt cap is reached, at which point the failure is escalated.

scenes.heading: Exponential backoff with jitter
scenes.narration: The delay doubles each attempt, so waits grow from half a second toward several seconds. The small random term is jitter, preventing many workers from retrying at the exact same instant. On the final attempt the error is re-raised, letting a higher layer decide what to do next.

scenes.text: Effective retries combine attempt caps, exponential backoff, jitter, and idempotency to recover from transient failures safely.
scenes.narration: Retries only help when the underlying operation is idempotent, so design for safe repetition before you add automatic re-attempts.
